tier_reason: First-party only: docs/COMPARISON_REPORT.md and docs/SCALING_NOTES.md time SuperLAME against the same LAME r6531 core run single-threaded on a Ryzen 7 5800X3D, and the engine build flags (clang 21.1.6, -O3 -march=znverN in build/build_dispatch.sh) are public, but no public script runs the stock-LAME comparison (tests/scaling.ps1 only compares SuperLAME thread counts with its own -t1), the baseline binary's flags are unstated and the test albums are commercial recordings, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'roughly 8x faster than stock single-threaded LAME at the same quality'; v1.1.0 on a Ryzen 7 5800X3D, 44-minute album, CBR 320: 13.8 s at 2 threads down to 3.9 s at 16 (~680x realtime), parallel efficiency ~93% at t2 and ~61% at t16 (no stock-LAME time is given for that run). docs/SCALING_NOTES.md (42-minute 440 MB album, mode not stated): stock LAME ~28 s versus SuperLAME ~3.6 s at -t2 to -t16, '~8x'; SuperLAME -t1 takes ~42 s (0.7x stock). docs/COMPARISON_REPORT.md (2026-06-29, pre-v1.1.0 build, 16 threads versus the same patched LAME r6531 core single-threaded, 4 albums): VBR -V2 5.84x to 6.17x (e.g. 4.19 s vs 24.46 s for a 50-minute album), CBR 320 1.49x to 4.73x (e.g. 17.19 s vs 25.60 s). The v1.1.0 CHANGELOG reports multithreaded encodes became 1.8x to 1.9x faster after that report (t16 7.2 s to 3.9 s on the 44-minute CBR 320 album), so the June table understates the current build.
corrections.workload: Multithreaded MP3 encoding of full albums (16-bit/44.1 kHz WAV) at VBR -V2 and CBR 320: SuperFast runs many libmp3lame instances on overlapping chunks and a serial repacker re-chains the bit reservoir. Measured with 16 threads on an 8-core/16-thread CPU against the same LAME r6531 core encoding single-threaded; the v1.1.0 scaling figures use the in-RAM --bench mode at 2 to 16 threads.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang 21.1.6 targeting x86_64-unknown-windows-msvc (Windows 11): libmp3lame engines built with -O3 -march=znver5 / znver4 / znver3 / x86-64 (build/build_dispatch.sh; znver3 engine used on the test CPU); frontend clang++ -std=c++17 -O2 -march=x86-64 and dr_flac clang -O2 -march=x86-64 (build/build_final.sh). Build flags of the stock-LAME baseline binary (build/phase2-build/lame.exe) are not stated.
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D (8 cores / 16 threads, Zen 3), Windows 11
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers only. The win comes from parallelism: 16 threads versus single-threaded stock LAME; per thread SuperLAME is slower (its -t1 is about 1.5x slower than stock LAME). No public script runs the stock-LAME comparison, the baseline binary's build flags are unstated and the test albums are commercial recordings, so the comparison cannot be reproduced. Multithreaded output is not bit-identical to stock LAME (decoded differences of -45 to -87 dB at chunk seams; single-thread output is identical). CBR gains are much smaller than VBR gains (1.49x to 4.73x versus 5.84x to 6.17x in the June report). The docs disagree on scaling: SCALING_NOTES says it plateaus at about 2 workers, while the v1.1.0 README shows gains up to 16 threads after the sleep-poll fix. Earlier builds had a repacker desync bug (fixed by porting fre:ac/BoCA fixes) and v1.1.1 fixed lost frames at low CBR bitrates. The znver4/znver5 engines are unverified; the build and tests are Windows-only (clang, PowerShell). Very new repo (3 stars). Built on LAME r6531 plus a port of fre:ac/BoCA SuperFast (GPL), not a GitHub fork.

notes: SuperLAME is a new multithreaded frontend that links four CPU-dispatched builds of LAME r6531 and ports Robert Kausch's fre:ac/BoCA SuperFast parallel-chunk encoder and bit-reservoir repacker; it is not a SIMD port of LAME. The baseline is the same LAME core single-threaded, so the speedup is thread-level parallelism (16 threads vs 1), not a faster encoder; I moved benchmark_url to the comparison report because the README never shows a stock-LAME time. Metadata checked on github.com: GPL-2.0-or-later, not a fork, last commit 2026-08-21 (v1.1.1).
